title: Lossless condensers with constant output overhead
formal:
Is there an explicit family of functions
\[\operatorname{Con}_{n,k}:\{0,1\}^{n}\times\{0,1\}^{d(n,k)}\to\{0,1\}^{m(n,k)}\]
and absolute integer constants \(C,\Delta\ge1\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge2\) and \(0\le k\le n\),
\[d(n,k)\le C\lceil\log_2 n\rceil,\qquad k+d(n,k)\le m(n,k)\le k+d(n,k)+\Delta,\]
and for every distribution \(X\) on \(n\)-bit strings with \(H_{\infty}(X)\ge k\), there is a distribution \(Y_X\) on \(m(n,k)\)-bit strings satisfying
\[H_{\infty}(Y_X)\ge k+d(n,k),\qquad \operatorname{TV}\bigl(\operatorname{Con}_{n,k}(X,U_{d(n,k)}),Y_X\bigr)\le1/100?\]
The seed is uniform and independent of \(X\). The family must have one deterministic polynomial-time evaluator for all parameters. This is the lossless-condenser formulation of Vadhan's Open Problem 6.35, paired in the source with the expander question 5.36.
why: A lossless condenser compresses an arbitrary weak source while preserving its available randomness. Constant output overhead would leave that randomness concentrated in a string only a constant number of bits longer than its entropy, using a short seed. In graph terms it asks for nearly collision-free expansion with an almost minimal number of right vertices, a useful resource in extraction and data structures.
status_note: Open Problems 5.36 and 6.35 and Proposition 6.33 were read on 2026-09-14. The bounded later check includes the full 2022 multiplicity-code condenser paper, the 9 September 2026 publication record for two-sided expansion, and that work’s full ECCC revision 2. These results do not supply constant output overhead with a logarithmic seed across the full entropy domain. No matching resolution was found; this is not an exhaustive current-openness certification.

sentences: A lossless condenser compresses a weak random source while preserving its guaranteed entropy together with the seed entropy.
This question asks for a logarithmic seed and an output only a constant number of bits longer than that preserved entropy.
The output may be nonuniform, but it must be within one hundredth in statistical distance of a distribution with the required min-entropy.
The equivalent graph target has nearly lossless expansion and only a constant factor more right vertices than the number of outgoing edges from a source set.
Recent multiplicity-code and two-sided-expansion results improve related structure without meeting this constant-overhead target.

definitions:
All lengths are integers in bits and all logarithms have base two. The min-entropy of a finite distribution is \(H_{\infty}(X)=-\log_2\max_x\Pr[X=x]\). The input promise therefore says that every point has probability at most \(2^{-k}\). Input distributions may be arbitrary; their coordinates need not be independent, and they need not have efficient samplers. The input to the condenser is a sample string and a seed, not a distribution description. \(U_t\) is uniform on all \(t\)-bit strings, with the single empty string when \(t=0\). Statistical distance is
\[\operatorname{TV}(P,Q)=\tfrac12\sum_z|P(z)-Q(z)|.\]
The comparison distribution \(Y_X\) may depend on the entire source distribution. Its existence is a mathematical guarantee; no algorithm for producing or sampling it is required.

Explicitness means that two fixed deterministic multitape Turing machines compute the lengths from \((1^n,k)\) and the full output from \((1^n,k,x,y)\), respectively. The entropy parameter is binary, \(|x|=n\), and \(|y|=d(n,k)\). For some fixed positive integers \(K,q\), each computation uses at most \(K(n+1)^q\) transitions, including preprocessing and output writing. No advice, oracle, randomized choice of construction or free length-dependent table is allowed. The machines and constants are fixed before \(n,k,X\); the comparison distribution is quantified after \(X\).

Lossless means that the comparison distribution preserves all \(k+d\) guaranteed input-and-seed entropy bits. The bounded quantity \(m-(k+d)\) is the output entropy gap, or output overhead, not lost entropy. The condenser is not required to output an almost-uniform string: it only has to be close to a distribution with the specified min-entropy. Uniformity conditional on a separately disclosed seed is not imposed.

There is an equivalent graph view for these parameters. Let \(N=2^n\), \(D=2^d\), \(M=2^m\), and \(K_0=2^k\). Treat the condenser as a neighbor function \([N]\times[D]\to[M]\), identifying integers with fixed-length binary strings. It defines a left-regular bipartite multigraph; seeds label edges, and repeated neighbors are permitted. The lossless condition is equivalent to requiring at least \((99/100)DK_0\) distinct neighbors for every set of exactly \(K_0\) left vertices. The size bounds become \(D\le(2n)^C\) and \(DK_0\le M\le2^{\Delta}DK_0\). Only this source-equivalent one-sided expansion is required; neither right-regularity nor right-to-left expansion is an additional condition.
answer_criterion: Provide a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof or refutation of the displayed uniform condenser-family claim. A construction must specify its algorithms and constants and establish all length, time, distance and entropy requirements over the entire domain. An equivalent graph construction qualifies with a proved translation to these guarantees. A negative answer must rule out every such family. A constant fraction of output entropy gap, a superlogarithmic seed, or a construction only for a restricted entropy regime does not meet the target.

context_blocks.text: Open Problem 5.36 asks for degree polynomial in \(\log N\), expansion \(0.99D\), and only \(O(K_0D)\) right vertices. Proposition 6.33 translates the powers-of-two case into lossless condensation. The card fixes the binary representation and the exact fixed-error condenser formulation of Open Problem 6.35.

The 2022 Kalev–Ta-Shma construction gives a different lossless condenser with logarithmic seed length. Its Theorem 2 allows an output entropy gap proportional to the source entropy, with parameter restrictions; it does not establish an absolute constant gap. The paper explicitly distinguishes entropy loss from entropy gap and describes small-gap extraction as an outstanding challenge.

The September 2026 paper proves that the Kalev–Ta-Shma graph also expands losslessly in the reverse direction and characterizes its expansion. This additional two-sided property concerns a different resource. Its stated right-side size still has a power loss relative to the source set size in the checked parameters, so it does not give the constant output overhead requested here.

The source relates a positive answer to improved extraction with constant total entropy loss, the separate target TCS-1015. A condenser is allowed a nonzero output entropy gap; an extractor instead asks that the output itself be close to uniform. The card preserves that distinction.
